From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Observability hooks & SDK integration - next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks for the context. Below is a compact integration reference tailored to Nova Retail's asks. Happy to jump on the call for a live walkthrough.

1) Auth options
- Short-lived API keys (recommended for initial proof-of-concept). Our platform supports signed JWTs and API keys with KMS-backed rotation. For enterprise Private deployments we support mTLS and HSM-backed key material.
- Recommended header: Authorization: Bearer <token>
- For signed JWTs: we support RS256 verification against your JWKS endpoint; tokens can include the x-redwood-tenant claim.

2) SDK quickstart (nodejs example)
- Install: npm i @redwood/inference
- Snippet:
  const {Client} = require('@redwood/inference');
  const client = new Client({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, baseUrl: 'https://api.redwood.ai' });
  const res = await client.chat.create({ model: 'rwd-chat-small', messages: [{role:'user', content:'Search for winter boots'}], routing: {priority:'latency'} });

3) Observability headers and propagation
- Trace id header: x-redwood-trace-id (we echo this back in responses)
- Parent span id (optional): x-redwood-parent-span
- Latency breakdown header: x-redwood-latency-ms (value is a comma-separated breakdown: queue_ms, model_infer_ms, network_ms)
- Token-cost header: x-redwood-token-usage (example: input=120,output=45,total=165)
- We also set x-redwood-model-version in responses so you can track rollouts.

4) Logging fields
- For request-side logs include: tenant_id, request_id, x-redwood-trace-id, model, route (e.g., dedicated/hosted), tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_usd

5) Embeddings & reranker guidance
- Two options:
  a) Keep embeddings in your vector DB (control, lower outbound egress). We recommend using our embeddings endpoint for creation and storing vectors in your store (Postgres+pgvector, Pinecone, etc.).
  b) Use Redwood-managed embeddings store for simpler ops (we provide versioning/refresh hooks). Tradeoffs: managed store simplifies refreshes but has egress costs and additional latency for very large corpora.
- Reranking: push a lightweight (few-shot) model to rerank top-K to reduce token usage for rerankers. We can provide a tuned config for Nova Retail's search query patterns.

6) Dashboards & alerts
- We'll share a pre-built Grafana/Datadog dashboard: per-route latency percentiles, token cost per request, failure rate, and model-version waterfall.
- Example alert: 95th percentile inference latency > 400ms for 5m window.

Attachments: observability_dashboard_proposal.png (dashboard mock), mutual_action_plan.docx (MAM with milestones)

Links:
- SDK quickstart: https://redwood.ai/docs/sdk-quickstart
- Dashboard mock: https://app.redwood.ai/dashboards/NR-OBS-3-proposal

Let me know if you want narrower header names or different breakdown formats — we can make them configurable per-account.
